newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN-AMRO to invest $137 mln in Hungary MHB bank.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO to invest $137 mln in Hungary MHB bank.

text.p: The Dutch banking group ABN AMRO on Wednesday announced it would invest $137 million in its new Hungarian acquisition, Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB).

"The priority for the ($137 million) will be automation and consumer banking," Michael J. Drabbe, chairman of ABN AMRO's international division, told Reuters after the signing ceremony of a deal by which the Dutch bank acquired an 89.23 percent stake in MHB for $89.23 million.
Hungary announced last month it had chosen ABN AMRO as the winner of a tender to buy the MHB stake ahead of a competing bid
The deal means that 85 percent of Hungary's banking sector has been privatised, the largest proportion in the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe.
The contract was signed in Budapest by officials of the two banks and Hungary's minister of finance Peter Medgyessy.
"ABN is a bank in which we find all the characteristics which make it an ideal partner for one of Hungary's largest banks," Medgyessy told reporters after the signing ceremony.
"This will ensure qualitative changes in terms of service and efficiency," he added.
The government plans to privatise Hungary's remaining banks, starting with K&H, Mezobank and Takarek Bank, within the next year, Medgyessy said.
"The signing of this deal shows the government is serious about bank privatisation," he added.
MHB is the fifth largest commercial bank in Hungary, with 70 branches across the country.

In preparation for the sell-off MHB introduced a rationalisation programme under chief executive officer Zsigmond Jarai, who took over in 1995, which saw it write off millions of dollars of bad debt, cut staff by 40 percent to 2,500 and reduce operating costs.
Drabbe said the banking network would be incorporated into ABN AMRO's worldwide network. The bank's new name has not yet benn chosen but it is sure to include the name of ABN AMRO, he said.
Drabbe said he saw a growing consumer sector in Hungary as European Union membership approaches.
"Hungary's position in our developemt of emerging markets is superb," he said. "Hungary will be a member of the EU and the synergy betwteen ABN AMRO and Hungary will grow phenomenally."
Drabbe added that corporate banking will also increase, with ABN AMRO serving to bring new investors to Hungary.
"That is where we have a lot of value to add -- structured finance, sophisticated products and investment banking that we'll bring in." he said.
